Regardless of how a avatar directory works, the one constant should be that all existing publicly uploaded avatars default to "Not Listed"
ANYTHING in such a directory should be 100% opt in per avatar. Nothing should be added to it automatically.

Additional concerns: Currently, paid avatars sold on sites like Gumroad and Booth often state that you may not upload the avatars as public. Sometimes this occurs anyway, though it is not a huge problem, even with it's put on a pedestal.
A public directory however, makes this even worse, as simply one person uploading a paid avatar publicly and having it be listed in a world allows the entire player base to use that paid avatar, without even needing to chance upon the world it's in.

@{5b4eb6697a870c3a5c2b0ca5|full_name}: Yeah. Unfortunately that's somewhat of an external issue that is exacerbated second-handedly by such a system, much like the crashers/rips issue. The only reason I wouldn't add it as a factor is that, at that point, there's not really much anyone can do to stop it due to how external it is.. It's tough to determine if it's better off just not having a 'for sale' filter at that point.. Because having it there would be very beneficial to some people, but just as likely to be detrimental.
And yeah, I added the 'not retroactive' bit as per what you said in the discord. The idea I have with it is, is to have the search allowance tickbox be right beside the public/private tickbox, so it's difficult to overlook if you're specifically deciding whether you want the avatar to be shareable or not.
Edit: I've added a note that specifies that the two options should be close together like that.
Edit2: I've re-structured and merged a couple points. Saying that an avatar is default to one thing or another during upload doesn't make sense with it being an option in the upload screen.

details:
I see that there are already a ton of 'please add an avatar search' posts, but none with specific details of how it could work in any particular detail. I'd like to fix that.
First, avatar search filters.
- By Name
- By Author
- By Tags (A new function for the SDK, similar to world tags.)
- By Location (Lists worlds with searchable avatars, and filters to those avatars when the world is selected.)
- By Newest (Avatars at the top would be the most recently made searchable, or most recently updated.)
- Additionally, a toggle between 'all, free, and sold', and allowing avatars to be marked with 'for sale' for avatars that are sold outside of the game. (**Caution:** This one has potential risks! While it benefits the makers to be able to 'advertise' their product, it also gives an easier way to find them as opportunities for malicious users to exploit how externally sold avatars are done.)
Now the specifics of how I think it should be handled.
- Avatars would NOT be directly accessible via this function. Players must go to the world that it is in and find it. This is to encourage the continued use of avatar worlds, and to allow for avatars that don't/can't show up on the search, to still be shared by proxy of avatars that do.
- Avatars that are not on a pedestal in a world but still set to searchable would only link to the author's profile or their worlds, not a specific world where the avatar is held.
- Whether an avatar is searchable or not would need to be an option in the SDK that is off by default. It would be alongside the public/private setting both in the upload screen and in the content manager, so that it's difficult to overlook when deciding if you want your avatar to be available or not, and easy to fix if you did.
- Avatars that were made prior to the update **should not be searchable by default**, to avoid any unintended side cases of being in a world but not intended to be shared outside of that, such as easter eggs, games, and immersive worlds.
- Avatars with a 'Very Poor' rating would not be searchable, the option would be greyed out. Both to encourage better design practices, and hamper the spread of their usage. To share these avatars they would have to exist in a world alongside other searchable avatars. (Preferably, these avatars would also not be directly cloneable, but that is another thing altogether.)
Preferably this function would be less of a priority than solutions for crasher avatars and avatar ripping.
- While a report function tied to avatar entries in the search would in part solve this, it would be much better to have things like cache encryption and anti-crashing measures in place, so that such avatars are less likely to be wider spread thanks to the function.
-
Hopefully that addresses most of the concerns surrounding the system and better outlines things to consider for implementation.
title: Avatar Search (And HOW Exactly)
